title: Designing an Online Bookstore
description: Build an online bookstore with catalog browsing, inventory management, shopping cart, checkout flow, and payment integration.

segments.text: An online bookstore seems simple until you think about concurrent purchases, inventory consistency, cart expiration, and payment failures. Let's build it right.
Core entities: Book with title, author, ISBN, and price. Catalog to browse and search. Inventory tracking stock counts. User with profile and address. Cart and Order to manage purchases.
The catalog service needs fast search. Support filtering by author, genre, price range, and rating. Under the hood, an inverted index or a search engine like Elasticsearch handles full-text queries.
Inventory management is where it gets tricky. Two users viewing the same book see 'one in stock.' Both click buy. Without proper concurrency control, you oversell. We need atomic stock decrements.

segments.thought_prompt: How would you prevent two users from buying the last copy of the same book simultaneously?

segments.text: The shopping cart holds items temporarily. Use optimistic locking: reserve stock when the user starts checkout, not when they add to cart. Set a reservation timeout to release abandoned holds.
Checkout is a multi-step process: validate cart items, calculate totals with tax and shipping, collect payment info, charge the payment gateway, and create the order. Each step can fail.
Payment integration uses the Strategy pattern. Stripe, PayPal, and credit card processors all implement a PaymentProcessor interface. The system picks the right strategy based on user selection.

Once payment succeeds, create an Order with status CONFIRMED. The order tracks items, shipping address, payment reference, and timestamps. Status transitions: confirmed, shipped, delivered, or cancelled.
Pulling it together: User has a Cart. Cart holds CartItems referencing Books. Checkout produces an Order. Order connects to Payment and ShippingInfo. Clean separation of concerns.

segments.thought_prompt: Payment succeeds but the order creation fails due to a database error. How do you handle this?

segments.text: You need idempotent operations and compensating transactions. Charge the card, and if order creation fails, issue a refund. The bookstore teaches you e-commerce fundamentals that apply to any online marketplace.
